response.sql: WITH mc AS (SELECT m.major_id, m.department, COUNT(*) AS member_count FROM member me JOIN major m ON me.link_to_major = m.major_id GROUP BY m.major_id, m.department), sh AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, member_count * 1.0 / (SELECT SUM(member_count) FROM mc) AS share FROM mc), da AS (SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, AVG(share) OVER (PARTITION BY department) AS dept_avg_share FROM sh) SELECT major_id, department, member_count, share, share - dept_avg_share AS diff_above_dept_avg FROM da WHERE share > dept_avg_share ORDER BY diff_above_dept_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Share = major's member count divided by the total number of members who have a matching major (members without a matching major are excluded from the denominator too).
Only majors with at least one member appear, so the department average is taken over those majors only (majors with zero members are not included).
Department average is the simple (unweighted) mean of its majors' shares.
